Summary of Changes
------------------

**Major Changes:**
* docs/clustermesh: overhaul Cluster Mesh documentation with a new introduction, improved load-balancing guidance, and Helm-first setup and certificate configuration instructions (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47615, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47351, @MrFreezeex)

**Minor Changes:**
* envoy: demote stale ADS endpoint warning (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47148, @nezdolik)
* Speed up recovery time for disrupted TCP connections that access a DSR-enabled Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47529, @julianwiedmann)

**Bugfixes:**
* azure: Stop issuing redundant CiliumNode status updates on every IPAM sync when the node's Azure interfaces are unchanged. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47449, @jaredledvina)
* bpf: dsr: don't look for TCP header on fragmented packets (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47640, @julianwiedmann)
* bpf: hostfw: tolerate unknown CT protocols and rely on policies (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47621, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47343, @smagnani96)
* clustermesh: fix MCS-API CRD install/upgrade when clustermesh-apiserver is started before the CRD version is actually installed (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47824, @MrFreezeex)
* datapath: turn ARP off on the base devices before bringing them up (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47838, @aanm)
* endpoint/watchdog: Avoid warning about endpoints being deleted (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47625, @christarazi)
* endpoint: Fix silent CIDR policy bypass and traffic drops after agent restart (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47880, @weizhoublue)
* envoy.httpUpstreamLingerTimeout accepts `0` as a chart value and templates into configmap. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47741, @jdw6359)
* envoy: restore http-idle-timeout as the route idle timeout source (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47583, @aanm)
* Fix a BPF verifier reject on pre-v5.12 kernels, when IPv6 is enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47765, @julianwiedmann)
* Fix a deadlock in the shutdown of Cilium operator related to CiliumEndpointSlices. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47967, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47802, @bimmlerd)
* Fix a NetworkPolicy update being ignored for up to two minutes when it arrived while an endpoint was waiting for its security identity to be resolved after a pod relabel. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47727, @aanm)
* Fix a spurious "unable to find ifindex for interface MAC" agent warning on EKS ENI IPAM by waiting for the ENI netlink interface before configuring ingress routes and rules. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47295, @aanm)
* Fix abnormal ip allocation caused by hostnetwork pod (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47552, @haozhangami)
* Fix unintended RevDNAT for client-to-pod TCP connections, when an identical connection was previously established through a DSR Service. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47881, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47593, @julianwiedmann)
* fix: allow setting endpointPolicyUpdateTimeoutDuration in helm (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47754, @weizhoublue)
* Fixed an issue where an HTTPRoute referencing a Gateway with mixed listener protocols (e.g. HTTP and TCP) was incorrectly rejected with `NotAllowedByListeners` when the TCP listener had an explicit `AllowedRoutes.Kinds` restriction. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46842, @pidreher)
* gateway-api/gamma: refresh CEC owner refs on route recreation (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47840, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: mark unresolved backend service ports in route status (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47766, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: preserve duplicate HTTPRoute rule precedence (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#46696, @thorn3r)
* gateway-api: prevent conflicted listeners from reaching ingestion (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47457, @asauber)
* gateway-api: requeue L4/TLS routes on ServiceImport updates (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47702, @mhofstetter)
* gateway-api: sync ListenerSet TLS secrets on ListenerSet events (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47627, @mhofstetter)
* ipcache: fix CIDR reference counter to use canonical prefixes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47208, @iwanhae)
* l2announcer: re-evaluate services on frontend changes (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47690, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47579, @mhofstetter)
* Log the correct route kind when the Gateway API operator fails to list TLSRoutes for a backend Service (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47826, @mehrdadbn9)
* operator: Emit startup logs in the configured log format (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47890, @HadrienPatte)
* Resolve a endpoint manager crash for restored endpoints with verbose policy logging enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47885, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47844, @bimmlerd)
* standalone-dns-proxy: return an error when no endpoint is found (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47954, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47791, @vipul-21)
* wireguard: Unsubscribe node handler on shutdown (Backport PR cilium/cilium#47805, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47614, @HadrienPatte)

signals.title: Support `hostname` in LB Service status
signals.text: Currently, Cilium will add rules for any addresses in the `status.loadBalancer.ingress.ip` stanza of relevant Loadbalancer Services. However, it's valid for Loadbalancer Services to use `status.loadBalancer.ingress.hostname` instead (AWS LB Services do this). In this case, we should be turning the hostname into IP addresses and adding those in the same ways that we add LB Service IPs currently. This is extra complicated because we'll need to maintain a watch on the hostname and update the IPs when the TTLs expire, which will probably require interaction with the DNS proxy. This issue covers figuring out what the best way forward is here, and then implementing something.

signals.title: Cilium HTTP L7 policies break HTTP proxy (CONNECT) connections
signals.text:
### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing issues ### What happened? When using HTTP L7 policies with an HTTP proxy (eg: when setting the `HTTP_PROXY` env-var for most programs), requests get mangled and usually end up being rejected by the HTTP proxy for some reason. This is pretty simple to reproduce: Deploy an HTTP proxy: ``` kubectl create ns test-proxy kubectl -n test-proxy create -f https://gist.githubusercontent.com/chancez/64411ad9f225bd24848cac4dafdd0b90/raw/758a2727a54c58558548a74b7eded6a459097c83/squid-deployment.yml ``` Run a workload that uses it: ``` kubectl -n test-proxy create -f https://gist.github.com/chancez/64411ad9f225bd24848cac4dafdd0b90/raw/758a2727a54c58558548a74b7eded6a459097c83/test-pod.yaml ``` Start observing flows in another terminal (setup your port-forward as needed): ``` hubble observe -f -n test-proxy ``` Notice that the requests are going from the test-client pod to the squid proxy, and squid proxy is making requests to the upstream (1.0.0.1). Example flow logs: ``` Mar 10 00:36:35.416: test-proxy/test-client:53540 (ID:42142) -> kube-system/coredns-565d847f94-6ctpg:53 (ID:30031) to-endpoint FORWARDED (UDP) Mar 10 00:36:35.417: test-proxy/test-client:53540 (ID:42142) <- kube-system/coredns-565d847f94-6ctpg:53 (ID:30031) to-endpoint FORWARDED (UDP) Mar 10 00:36:35.420: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) -> test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN) Mar 10 00:36:35.420: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) <- test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: SYN, ACK) Mar 10 00:36:35.420: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) -> test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK) Mar 10 00:36:35.420: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) -> test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK, PSH) Mar 10 00:36:35.420: test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:34654 (ID:59769) -> 1.0.0.1:80 (world) to-stack FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK, PSH) Mar 10 00:36:35.421: test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:34654 (ID:59769) <- 1.0.0.1:80 (world) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK) Mar 10 00:36:35.424: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) <- test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK, PSH) Mar 10 00:36:35.426: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) <- test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK, FIN) Mar 10 00:36:35.426: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) -> test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK) Mar 10 00:36:35.426: test-proxy/test-client:41190 (ID:42142) -> test-proxy/squid-deployment-778cc7c55c-4mv4m:3128 (ID:59769) to-endpoint FORWARDED (TCP Flags: ACK, FIN) ``` You can also check the test-client pods, and you should see an HTTP 301 redirect (from http signals.title: bpf: migrate non-branching config macros to runtime configuration
signals.text: The current step in the clang-freedom (pre-compiled eBPF programs) journey is to start transitioning compile time configuration to load-time (runtime) configuration. The necessary agent and loader infrastructure has been merged. Runtime configuration can be defined with [`DECLARE_CONFIG` and `NODE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/static_data.h). See [Configuring the Datapath](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/contributing/development/datapath_config) in the Cilium Developer docs for guidelines and principles. ~~This issue specifically tracks variables which do not influence control flow by enabling or disabling certain code paths. Variables used in `#ifdef`/`#if` and `if(is_defined(...))` will be converted in 1.19 since dead code elimination only really landed in Linux 5.5, and Cilium 1.18 targets Linux 5.4 which will go EOL at the end of 2025.~~ 1.19 targets Linux 5.10. We can migrate branching macros, too. Additionally, https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/41628 shipped in 1.19 which added dead code detection in the agent to avoid loading unused maps and tail calls. Branching macros can now safely be ported. This issue is for migrating `node_config.h` and `WriteNodeConfig` entries to `config.Node`, as well as some leftover per-object configs in `ep_config.h`. Through this issue, we can coordinate work and keep an overview. If you want to work on a particular (set of) variable(s), drop a comment and we'll spin out an issue or assign you to a list item. The list may change over time and may grow as we find more work in this category. When migrating variables, do a quick search through [Paul's macro documentation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/15379#issuecomment-897441189) for a good docstring to use in `DECLARE_CONFIG`. - [ep_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/ep_config.h) - [x] HOST_EP_ID - [x] DIRECT_ROUTING_DEV_IFINDEX - [node_config.h](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/node_config.h) - [x] CLUSTER_ID - [x] CILIUM_*_IFINDEX, CILIUM_*_MAC (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43474) - [x] TUNNEL_PORT, TUNNEL_PROTOCOL (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43520) - [x] KERNEL_HZ, ENABLE_JIFFIES (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] L2_ANNOUNCEMENTS(_MAX_LIVENESS) (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42587) - [x] EPHEMERAL_MIN (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43564) - [x] IS_L3_DEV, NATIVE_DEV_MAC_BY_IFINDEX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/39116 & https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] CLUSTER_ID_MAX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/42478) - [x] IDENTITY_{LEN,MAX} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43507) - [x] VTEP_MASK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43112) - [x] NODEPORT_PORT_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43680) - [x] IPV4_LOOPBACK (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/38818) - [x] NAT_46X64_PREFIX (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/43799) - [x] CIDR_IDENTITY_RANGE_{START,END} (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44223) - [x] HASH_INIT{4,6}_SEED (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44190) - [x] EVENTS_MAP_* (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/44795) - [ ] VLAN_FILTER (https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38721) - [x] Reserved security IDs (HOST_ID, WORLD_ID, ect.) signals.title: BPF masquerading: Traffic to ExternalIP node addresses is masqueraded
signals.text: When using BPF masquerading, traffic to ExternalIP and InternalIP node addresses is not masqueraded by default. That was reported at https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/17177 previously and https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/37568 added a new flag, `enable-remote-node-masquerade`, to masquerade traffic to both ExternalIP and InternalIP node addresses. This isn't consistent with our iptables-based masquerading however. In that mode, we only masquerade traffic to ExternalIP addresses and assume traffic to InternalIP addresses is always routable. An additional optimization, making things consistent between the two modes, would distinguish ExternalIP and InternalIP addresses in the datapath to only masquerade traffic to ExternalIP addresses. We can probably achieve that via the node ID map.

signals.title: NodePort reverse NAT can prefer a fully closed TUPLE_F_OUT entry over a live direct TUPLE_F_IN entry after tuple collision
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? A completed NodePort connection can leave a fully closed `TUPLE_F_OUT` conntrack entry whose post-DNAT 5-tuple collides with a new direct connection to the same backend. Although the two conntrack entries are distinct map keys because one uses `TUPLE_F_OUT` and the other `TUPLE_F_IN`, a backend response does not carry the tuple flag. The NodePort reverse-NAT lookup can therefore select the stale `TUPLE_F_OUT` entry and incorrectly reverse-DNAT a response belonging to the live direct connection. This caused a connectivity-test failure during a Cilium upgrade/downgrade CI run at: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/actions/runs/29779009002/job/88475528839. The failed request timed out while connecting from *a node not managed by Cilium*: ```text client: fc00:c111::2 backend: fd00:10:244:1::1782:8080 ``` ## Sequence leading to the collision The test first made a successful NodePort request and then made a direct request to the selected backend pod. The NodePort frontend was: ```text [fc00:c111::5]:32397 ``` The selected backend was: ```text [fd00:10:244:1::1782]:8080 ``` Both the NodePort frontend and the backend were on the same Cilium node, while the client was an external pod on a different node. The first connection was: ```text Client-visible NodePort tuple: TCP [fc00:c111::2]:56490 -> [fc00:c111::5]:32397 ``` After NodePort DNAT, the backend-visible tuple was: ```text TCP [fc00:c111::2]:56490 -> [fd00:10:244:1::1782]:8080 ``` That connection completed normally. About 1 second later, the client reused source port `56490` for a direct connection: ```text Client-visible direct tuple: TCP [fc00:c111::2]:56490 -> [fd00:10:244:1::1782]:8080 ``` This source-port reuse is valid from the client TCP stack's perspective because the destinations of the two client-visible connections differ: ```text NodePort destination: [fc00:c111::5]:32397 Direct destination: [fd00:10:244:1::1782]:8080 ``` However, after the NodePort connection was DNATed, both connections had exactly the same backend-visible 5-tuple. The direct connection exchanged SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK packets, followed by resets/retransmitted SYN-ACKs, and eventually timed out. ## Conntrack evidence The conntrack dump from the failed CI run contained all of the relevant entries. The completed NodePort connection had a service entry: ```text TCP SVC fc00:c111::2:56490 -> fc00:c111::5:32397 [RxClosing TxClosing] RevNAT=217 BackendID=35 ``` Its post-DNAT NodePort entry was: ```text TCP OUT fc00:c111::2:56490 -> fd00:10:244:1::1782:8080 [RxClosing TxClosing ... NodePort] RevNAT=217 ``` The new direct connection had: ```text TCP IN fc00:c111::2:56490 -> fd00:10:244:1::1782:8080 RevNAT=0 ``` Thus the address, port, and protocol portions of the `TUPLE_F_OUT` and `TUPLE_F_IN` keys were identical. Only the tuple flag distinguished the entries. The NodePort `TUPLE_F_OUT` entry was already fully closed, while the direct `TUPLE_F_IN` entry represented the new live connection. ## Why this is ambiguous For the backend response: ```text TCP [fd00:10:244:1::1782]:8080 -> [fc00:c111::2]:56490 ``` there is no information in the packet indicating whether it belongs to the old NodePort flow or the new direct flow. `TUPLE_F_IN` and `TUPLE_F_OUT` are conntrack lookup namespaces, not packet-carried metadata. Due to the backend TCP stack seeing the same TCP tuple for both connections, it is not possible for both of these connections to be alive at the same time. In this case the NodePort connection was fully closed, while only the direct connection was live. ## Conditions required This specific failure can occur when: 1. A client connects to a NodePort. 2. The NodePort selects a backend local to the NodePort ingress node. 3. The client source address and port are preserved on the local-backend path. 4. The connection closes, but its fully closed NodePort `TUPLE_F_OUT` entry remains in the CT map. 5. The client starts a direct connection to that backend and legally reuses the same source port because its original destination differs from the NodePort destination. 6. The new direct connection's `TUPLE_F_IN` key collides with the post-DNAT NodePort tuple. 7. NodePort reverse-NAT lookup uses the fully closed `TUPLE_F_OUT` entry for a response belonging to the live direct connection. A remote NodePort backend normally avoids this exact arrangement because NodePort state and backend ingress state reside on different nodes, and the normal remote-backend SNAT path changes the source tuple. DSR, hybrid, and other source-preserving modes may require a separate audit. ## Possible fix When the two interpretations collide, favor an open `TUPLE_F_IN` entry over a fully closed NodePort `TUPLE_F_OUT` entry. Conceptually, NodePort reverse-NAT should be suppressed when: ```text matching TUPLE_F_OUT: NodePort entry RxClosing && TxClosing and matching TUPLE_F_IN: present and not fully closed ``` Active or half-closed NodePort connections should retain the existing reverse-NAT behavior. The special case should be limited to a fully closed NodePort entry competing with a live direct entry. It may also be possible to expire or remove the fully closed `TUPLE_F_OUT` entry when this collision is detected, but merely preferring the live entry may be the less invasive first fix. Since the observed failure was IPv6 but the IPv4 and IPv6 lookup paths are analogous, both families should be covered. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Create kind and install Cilium with relevant settings ``` make kind cilium install \ --version v1.20.0-rc.0 \ --wait \ --helm-set=ipam.mode=kubernetes \ --helm-set=ipv4.enabled=true \ --helm-set=ipv6.enabled=true \ --helm-set-string=kubeProxyReplacement=true \ --helm-set-string=routingMode=native \ --helm-set-string=autoDirectNodeRoutes=true \ --helm-set-string=ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR=10.244.0.0/16 \ --helm-set-string=ipv6NativeRoutingCIDR=fd00:10:244::/56 \ --helm-set=bpf.masquerade=true \ --helm-set-string=loadBalancer.mode=snat \ --helm-set=devices=eth0 cilium status --wait --wait-duration=5m ``` 2. Let the connectivity test create echo backends and NodePorts ``` cilium connectivity test --test no-policies ``` 3. Resolve a backend and its local NodePort frontend ``` REPRO_NS=cilium-test-1 REPRO_CLIENT_IPV6=fc00:c111::10 REPRO_SOURCE_PORT=45681 REPRO_POD_CIDR6=fd00:10:244::/56 REPRO_CURL_IMAGE=quay.io/cilium/alpine-curl:v1.10.0 REPRO_BACKEND_POD=$(kubectl -n "$REPRO_NS" get pod \ -l name=echo-other-node \ -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') REPRO_BACKEND_NODE=$(kubectl -n "$REPRO_NS" get pod "$REPRO_BACKEND_POD" \ -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}') REPRO_BACKEND_NODE=$(kubectl -n "$REPRO_NS" get pod "$REPRO_BACKEND_POD" \ -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}') REPRO_BACKEND_IPV6=$(kubectl -n "$REPRO_NS" get pod "$REPRO_BACKEND_POD" -o json | jq -r '.status.podIPs[].ip | select(contains(":"))') REPRO_NODE_IPV6=$(kubectl get node "$REPRO_BACKEND_NODE" -o json | jq -r '.status.addresses[] | select(.type == "InternalIP") | .address | select(contains(":"))') REPRO_NODEPORT=$(kubectl -n "$REPRO_NS" get service echo-other-node \ -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].nodePort}') REPRO_CILIUM_POD=$(kubectl -n kube-system get pod \ -l k8s-app=cilium \ --field-selector="spec.nodeName=$REPRO_BACKEND_NODE" \ -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') echo "client=[$REPRO_CLIENT_IPV6]:$REPRO_SOURCE_PORT" echo "nodeport=[$REPRO_NODE_IPV6]:$REPRO_NODEPORT" echo "backend=[$REPRO_BACKEND_IPV6]:8080" echo "backend-node=$REPRO_BACKEND_NODE" ``` 4. Clear old CT state ``` kubectl -n kube-system exec "$REPRO_CILIUM_POD" -- \ cilium-dbg bpf ct flush ``` 5. Complete the NodePort connection ``` docker run --rm \ --network kind-cilium \ --ip6 "$REPRO_CLIENT_IPV6" \ --cap-add NET_ADMIN \ --entrypoint /bin/sh \ "$REPRO_CURL_IMAGE" \ -c "ip -6 route replace $REPRO_POD_CIDR6 via $REPRO_NODE_IPV6 && curl -gSs --fail \ --connect-timeout 2 \ --max-time 5 \ --local-port $REPRO_SOURCE_PORT \ -H 'Connection: close' \ http://[$REPRO_NODE_IPV6]:$REPRO_NODEPORT/ \ -o /dev/null" ``` 6. Reuse the tuple for a direct Pod-IP connection ``` if docker run --rm \ --network kind-cilium \ --ip6 "$REPRO_CLIENT_IPV6" \ --cap-add NET_ADMIN \ --entrypoint /bin/sh \ "$REPRO_CURL_IMAGE" \ -c "ip -6 route replace $REPRO_POD_CIDR6 via $REPRO_NODE_IPV6 && curl -gSsv --fail \ --connect-timeout 2 \ --max-time 5 \ --local-port $REPRO_SOURCE_PORT \ -H 'Connection: close' \ http://[$REPRO_BACKEND_IPV6]:8080/ \ -o /dev/null" then echo "UNEXPECTED: direct connection succeeded" else REPRO_DIRECT_STATUS=$? echo "Reproduced: direct connection failed with exit $REPRO_DIRECT_STATUS" fi ``` - Expected result: ``` curl: (28) Failed to connect ... Timeout was reached Reproduced: direct connection failed with exit 28 ``` - Inspect the collision: ``` kubectl -n kube-system exec "$REPRO_CILIUM_POD" -- \ cilium-dbg bpf ct list global | rg "$REPRO_SOURCE_PORT" ``` ### Cilium Version v1.20.0-rc.0 ### Kernel Version Linux lima-dev 6.17.0-35-generic #35~24.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue May 26 19:14:16 UTC 2 aarch64 aarch64 aarch64 GNU/Linux ### Kubernetes Version Client Version: v1.34.1 Kustomize Version: v5.7.1 Server Version: v1.32.0 Warning: version difference between client (1.34) and server (1.32) exceeds the supported minor version skew of +/-1 ### Regression Not known to be a regression, likely has always failed like this. ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Split-Stage Deterministic NAT for egress gateway.
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? Current egress gateway implementation uses a single point of NAT node and faces the problem of single node scaling (can be solved using different gw for different targets), and redundancy problem as all gateways need synchronize their connection tables. Reling on a single egress gateway makes it harder to implement if the external traffic is so critical. Why we want to do this: - increase scalability using multiple active-active gateways. - minimal effect when switching between egress gateways. ### Describe the feature you'd like The solution or idea comes from [rfc6346](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6346) **Outbound, From POD to the related external traffic:** - Stage-1 : Node converts related extenal traffic onto the egress ip and port block calculated with deterministic CGNAT formula. It converts POD's ephemeral source port to an unsed port from the port block using conn track tables. It also changes the source port to the calculated egress ip. Then forwards traffic via tunnel to a egress gateway. - Stage-2 : Egress gateway accepts the packet and forwards it to the outside as source port and source address are already changed. **Inbound, From External to the POD (Response):** - Stage-2: Egress gateway looks at destination port and ip. It finds the responsible node from the deterministic CGNAT formula and then tunnels traffic to it. This gives ability to run multiple gateways. Return traffic can hit any of them and it will forward packet to the responsible node. - Stage-1: Node forwards the packet to the POD using conntrack table. ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signals.title: v1.19.3: WireGuard handshakes never complete on any node pair (tunnel/geneve + DSR), all cross-node pod traffic dead, on Oracle Linux only.
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? After upgrading to Cilium 1.19.3, all cross-node pod-to-pod connectivity is dead cluster-wide. The root symptom is that the WireGuard handshake never completes between *any* pair of nodes, in *either* direction. Every node reports, for every one of its 5 peers: ``` latest handshake: 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z transfer: 0 B received, 9836672 B sent ``` ``` 96: cilium_wg0: <POINTOPOINT,NOARP,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1300 ... RX: bytes packets errors dropped missed mcast 0 0 0 0 0 0 TX: bytes packets errors dropped carrier collsns 44358560 299720 0 2162782 0 0 ``` `cilium-dbg status` shows host connectivity is healthy while the encrypted overlay is completely dead: ``` Cluster health: 1/6 reachable (2026-07-28T13:02:11Z) cl-13-kubesi-worker-0: Host connectivity to 10.47.2.203: ICMP to stack: OK, RTT=297.168µs HTTP to agent: OK, RTT=961.602µs Endpoint connectivity to 10.42.2.197: ICMP to stack: Connection timed out HTTP to agent: Get "http://10.42.2.197:4240/hello": context deadline exceeded ``` With `echo module wireguard +p > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control` on `controlplane-1`: (pattern repeats like this, no 'receiving' alike messages) ``` [427001.163104] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 3 (10.47.2.217:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 11) [427001.163232] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Sending handshake initiation to peer 3 (10.47.2.217:51871) [427001.175653] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Sending handshake initiation to peer 1 (10.47.2.194:51871) [427004.235068] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 5 (10.47.3.11:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 2) [427006.284042] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 3 (10.47.2.217:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 12) [427006.284054] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 2 (10.47.2.203:51871) did not complete after 5 seconds, retrying (try 18) [427023.178883] wireguard: cilium_wg0: Handshake for peer 2 (10.47.2.203:51871) did not complete after 20 attempts, giving up ``` I ran claude on this, here's the output: ## What I have already ruled out I did a fairly deep investigation before filing. The following are all **not** the cause: | Hypothesis | Evidence against | |---|---| | **Public key mismatch** | All 6 nodes' live interface keys match their `CiliumNode` `network.cilium.io/wg-pub-key` annotations exactly, and match the corresponding peer entries on other nodes | | **Wrong endpoints / allowed-ips** | Each peer has `endpoint: <nodeIP>:51871` and `allowed ips: <nodeIP>/32`, which is correct for tunnel mode (geneve-encapsulated outer packet) | | **Clock skew (TAI64N replay rejection)** | Node clocks agree within ~1.8s | | **Cilium BPF dropping packets** | `cilium-dbg monitor --type drop -v` shows nothing during reproduction; `cilium-dbg bpf metrics list` shows no drop reasons other than an unrelated `Unsupported L3 protocol` on IPv6 RouterSolicitation | | **Issue #46100 (fragment tracking)** | No `DROP_FRAG_NOT_FOUND` counter present on any node. Handshake initiations are 148 B, far below any MTU | | **Host firewall** | `iptables` OUTPUT rule `ACCEPT all -- 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.0/8 state NEW` covers node-to-node traffic (2.7M packets); no DROP rule counter increments during reproduction | | **rp_filter** | `IPReversePathFilter` stays at 0 across bursts (note: `enp1s0/rp_filter=1`, `all=0`, so effective strict — but it is demonstrably not dropping these) | | **Network fabric blocking UDP** | Disproved by measurement — see below | | **Socket not bound / socket drops** | `ss -unlp` shows `UNCONN 0.0.0.0:51871`; `/proc/net/udp` shows `drops=0` for that socket | ### Measurement showing UDP does traverse the fabric Sending synthetic UDP bursts node-to-node (`worker-0` → `worker-1`, both `10.47.2.0/24`): - Receiver NIC counter (`/proc/net/dev`, counted before BPF): `5,603,727 → 5,608,812` = **+5,085 for 5,000 datagrams sent**. Packets reach the wire and the NIC. - Receiver netfilter INPUT hook, diffing `iptables-save -c` around a 3,000-packet burst to port 51871: ``` DELTA=3371 filter [27595:1956942] -A INPUT -m comment --comment "cilium-feeder: CILIUM_INPUT" -j CILIUM_INPUT DELTA=3361 filter [9070529:4141298931] -A INPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL DELTA=3371 raw -A PREROUTING -j CILIUM_PRE_raw DELTA=3371 mangle -A PREROUTING -j CILIUM_PRE_mangle DELTA=2999 nat -A PREROUTING -j CILIUM_PRE_nat ``` So synthetic UDP to 51871 is routed for local delivery and passes netfilter without being dropped. Node-to-node TCP and ICMP work normally throughout (confirmed by Cilium's own health prober, RTT ~0.3–1 ms). So: the path carries UDP, the keys are right, nothing visibly drops the packets, and yet no peer ever answers a handshake initiation. ### How can we reproduce the issue? Surprisingly: this setup **works** on Ubuntu-based setup, I found this to be broken only on Oracle Linux 1. RKE2 cluster, 6 nodes (3 control-plane, 3 workers), Oracle Linux 9.8 / UEK kernel. 2. Cilium 1.19.3 with the config below: `routing-mode: tunnel` + `tunnel-protocol: geneve`, `encryption.type=wireguard` (nodeEncryption disabled), kube-proxy replacement with `loadBalancer.mode=dsr` and `dsrDispatch=geneve`. 3. Physical NIC MTU 9000 (happens on different clusters with "regular" MTU of 1500 too) , Cilium `MTU: 1380` (yields `cilium_wg0` MTU 1300). 4. Observe `cilium-dbg debuginfo | grep -A5 'peer:'`, all peers show `latest handshake: 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` and `0 B received`. Relevant Helm values: ```yaml MTU: 1380 encryption: enabled: true type: wireguard tunnelProtocol: geneve kubeProxyReplacement: true loadBalancer: algorithm: maglev dsrDispatch: geneve mode: dsr bpf: masquerade: true hostLegacyRouting: false localRedirectPolicies: enabled: true pmtuDiscovery: enabled: true # or false, doesn't matter, both yield same outcome ``` ### Cilium Version `Cilium: Ok 1.19.3 (v1.19.3-f5eb641b)` ### Kernel Version ``` 5.15.0-322.203.3.4.el9uek.x86_64 ``` ### Kubernetes Version ``` 1.35 (v1.35.5+rke2r2) [linux/amd64] ``` ### Regression Yes. This cluster worked before the upgrade to Cilium 1.19 (version: v1.18.3). Connectivity broke at the upgrade. WireGuard has never completed a single handshake in the current agents' lifetime (4d+ uptime, `latest handshake: never`). ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell KubeProxyReplacement: True [enp1s0 10.47.3.11 fe80::21a:4aff:fe16:1c4 10.47.17.1 (Direct Routing)] CNI Chaining: portmap Cilium: Ok 1.19.3 (v1.19.3-f5eb641b) IPAM: IPv4: 14/126 allocated from 10.42.0.128/25 Routing: Network: Tunnel [geneve] Host: BPF Attach Mode: Legacy TC Device Mode: veth Masquerading: BPF [enp1s0] 10.42.0.128/25 [IPv4: Enabled, IPv6: Disabled] Controller Status: 86/86 healthy Encryption: Wireguard [NodeEncryption: Disabled, cilium_wg0 (Pubkey: 7we7...fjk8=, Port: 51871, Peers: 5)] Cluster health: 1/6 reachable Modules Health: Stopped(23) Degraded(0) OK(113) ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Option to disable Prometheus annotations in Helm Chart
signals.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? Datadog has a Cilium integration that makes Cilium metrics free. This is great, as custom metrics are expensive and Cilium has a lot of metrics. However, the Prometheus metrics port needs to be present for the integration to work but in the Helm Chart it is not possible to enable the port without also enabling the Prometheus scraping annotations. This means that the datadog agent picks up the scraping annotations and sends all of the metrics to Datadog as custom metrics in addition to the metrics coming from the integration. ### Describe the feature you'd like I would like an option in the helm chart to disable Prometheus Scraping Annotations but not disable the metrics port. ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signals.title: Netkit + endpointRoutes + hostNamespaceOnly reclassifies service replies as new flows
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.20.0 and lower than v1.21.0 ### What happened? I built a new single node cluster using "modern Cilium settings" and Tailscale Operator. The specific problematic settings are the combination of: - `bpf.datapathMode=netkit` - `endpointRoutes.enabled=true` - `socketLB.hostNamespaceOnly=true` ([required for Tailscale operator](https://tailscale.com/docs/kubernetes-operator/reference/compatibility#cilium-kube-proxy-replacement-mode)) The behaviours I saw included: - Hubble showing ephemeral source ports as destination ports - Cilium network policies would match the beginning of a connection (SYN) but not thereafter, causing traffic to fail unless I disabled network policies ### How can we reproduce the issue? Install cilium: ``` helm upgrade --install cilium cilium/cilium \ --namespace kube-system \ --version "$CILIUM_VERSION" \ --wait --timeout 10m \ --set image.repository="$CILIUM_IMAGE_REPO" \ --set image.tag="$CILIUM_IMAGE_TAG" \ --set image.useDigest=false \ --set image.pullPolicy=Always \ --set operator.image.repository="$CILIUM_OPERATOR_IMAGE_REPO" \ --set operator.image.tag="$CILIUM_IMAGE_TAG" \ --set operator.image.useDigest=false \ --set ipam.mode=kubernetes \ --set ipv6.enabled=true \ --set ipv4.enabled=true \ --set bpf.masquerade=true \ --set bpf.datapathMode=netkit \ --set bandwidthManager.enabled=true \ --set bandwidthManager.bbr=true \ --set bpf.distributedLRU.enabled=true \ --set bpfClockProbe=true \ --set endpointRoutes.enabled=true \ --set routingMode=native \ --set devices=enp2s0f0 \ --set ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR="$NATIVE_ROUTING_CIDR_V4" \ --set ipv6NativeRoutingCIDR="$NATIVE_ROUTING_CIDR_V6" \ --set bgpControlPlane.enabled=true \ --set nodePort.enabled=true \ --set operator.replicas=1 \ --set kubeProxyReplacement=true \ --set socketLB.hostNamespaceOnly=true \ --set securityContext.capabilities.ciliumAgent="{CHOWN,KILL,NET_ADMIN,NET_RAW,IPC_LOCK,SYS_ADMIN,SYS_RESOURCE,DAC_OVERRIDE,FOWNER,SETGID,SETUID}" \ --set securityContext.capabilities.cleanCiliumState="{NET_ADMIN,SYS_ADMIN,SYS_RESOURCE}" \ --set k8sServiceHost=localhost \ --set k8sServicePort=7445 \ --set cgroup.autoMount.enabled=false \ --set cgroup.hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup \ --set hubble.relay.enabled=true \ --set hubble.relay.replicas=1 \ --set hubble.ui.enabled=true \ --set hubble.ui.replicas=1 \ --set hubble.preferIpv6=true ``` 2. Deploy some containers. 3. Watch Hubble UI. Note how ingress traffic shows with destination port = ephemeral port ranges. These are the reply packets creating new sessions. 4. Add filters between components. A correctly designed strict filter will cause traffic to fail because the reply packets create new sessions. Please see attached screenshot from Hubble UI: ### Cilium Version v1.20.0 and main ### Kernel Version 6.18.42 on Talos 1.13.8 ### Kubernetes Version 1.36.2 ### Regression No known regression ### Sysdump Did not capture before developing the patch -- if this is truly important I can provide. ### Relevant log output ```shell `cilium-dbg monitor -v` with `Debug` and `DebugLB`. One flow, client ep 860 (`::7245`) → service `fd00:10:96::334c:3003`, backend ep 742 (`::8c2`): FROM 742 Attempting local delivery for container id 860 from seclabel 35952 FROM 860 CT lookup src=[::0:8c2]:3003 dst=[::0:7245]:34386 backend src FROM 860 CT verdict: Reply, revnat=42 FROM 860 Reverse NAT lookup, index=42 FROM 860 Performing reverse NAT, address.p4=4c330000 port=3003 -> endpoint 860 ... state reply ... [fd00:10:96::334c]:3003 -> ...:34386 FROM 860 Inheriting identity=35952 from stack FROM 860 CT lookup src=[::0:334c]:3003 dst=[::0:7245]:34386 service src FROM 860 CT verdict: New, revnat=42 FROM 860 Attempting local delivery for container id 860 from seclabel 21986 FROM 860 Conntrack create: proxy-port=0 revnat=0 src-identity=35952 -> endpoint 860 ... state new ... orig-ip fd00:10:96::334c The egress CT entry is created post-DNAT, keyed on the backend, so the service-addressed packet cannot match it: TCP OUT 172.31.32.4:59946 -> 172.31.32.140:3003 RevNAT=76 TCP SVC 172.31.32.4:59946 -> 10.111.71.201:3003 RevNAT=76 BackendID=160 ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [x] Are you a user of Cilium? signals.title: Host firewall: policy-selected node is permanently isolated after reboot — host endpoint policy map ends up deny-all (cold boot, audit-off flip) or allow-all (runtime label add), never the computed policy
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? Closest match is #25448 ("host firewall drops reply traffic for legitimate connections when policies are first enforced"). This report is a stronger manifestation of what looks like the same enforcement-transition problem: in our setup the drop window is not transient — it is fatal and self-sustaining (node permanently isolated until out-of-band reboot), it reproduces on every cold boot, and it also reproduces on a fully synced agent when audit mode is switched off at runtime. Filing separately because the evidence points at the host endpoint's BPF policy map never receiving the computed allow entries, with three distinct end states depending on the path taken. ## What happened? Environment: Cilium 1.18.6 (kubespray), host firewall enabled, kube-proxy replacement enabled, VXLAN tunnel, WireGuard node encryption, `bpf-datapath-mode: netkit`, CRD identity mode, 61 nodes. A `CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy` with `nodeSelector` on worker nodes provides ingress lock-down (fromEntities cluster/remote-node/health/host, SSH/ICMP via CiliumCIDRGroup refs plus literal CIDRs, kubelet/NodePort from cluster). **1. Cold boot of a selected node → permanent isolation.** ~13 s after cilium-agent starts, every packet in and out is dropped as `Policy denied` by `bpf_host.c:865`. The node never recovers: the agent needs the apiserver to finish its sync, and its own egress to the apiserver is what is being dropped. Captured from inside a locked node (systemd unit dumping via crictl exec): - at agent start, `cilium-dbg endpoint list` is still **empty** (host endpoint not created yet) while bpf_host is already attached and enforcing deny-by-default with an empty policy map; - 105 659 `Policy denied` drops in 20 s, 73 018 of them the node's own egress to the apiserver LB: `identity host->unknown: <node-ip>:* -> <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443`; - at that moment the BPF ipcache is fully populated (8 292 entries) and local CIDR identities for the policy's allowed CIDRs are already allocated — e.g. ICMP from an explicitly allowed CIDR is dropped with its allocated identity (`identity 16777222->unknown`). The policy is computed; its allow entries are just not in the host endpoint policy map. **2. Runtime audit-off flip on a fully synced agent → same isolation.** Boot the node with `policy-audit-mode: true` (per-node CiliumNodeConfig): node comes up healthy, host endpoint reaches `state=ready`, realized policy has all 8 L4 ingress rules, `enforcement=audit-ingress`. Then `cilium-dbg endpoint config <hostep> PolicyAuditMode=Disabled` → "configuration updated successfully" → the node is fully isolated within seconds. The agent log ends abruptly mid incremental `UpdatePolicyMaps` processing with no error line — consistent with the deny default being installed while the allow entries never land. **3. Warm enforcement via label add → policy map silently allow-all.** With the agent fully synced and the node label added at runtime (CCNP starts selecting the node), the endpoint reports `enforcement=ingress`, but `cilium-dbg bpf policy get <hostep>` contains only the wildcard pair (`Allow Ingress ANY` prefix 0 / `Allow Egress ANY` prefix 0) — i.e. no actual enforcement. This is the only transition that leaves the node reachable, and it appears to do so by not programming the policy at all. For contrast, a long-running node whose agent processed the CCNP incrementally while already enforcing has a fully programmed map (per-identity allows, port ranges) — so the policy→map pipeline itself works. So the same policy, same version, produces three different host endpoint policy-map end states depending on the transition path: deny-all (cold boot, audit-off flip), allow-all (runtime label add), correct (incremental update on an already-enforcing endpoint). Datapath mode does not appear to matter: a cold boot with `bpf-datapath-mode: veth` (per-node CiliumNodeConfig) locked out identically (caveat: the override's application could not be positively confirmed from inside the locked node). Impact: any reboot of a policy-selected node isolates it permanently; recovery requires out-of-band console/rescue access. 54 nodes affected in our cluster. ## Cilium Version 1.18.6 ## Kernel Version 6.8.0-124-generic (Ubuntu 24.04) ## Kubernetes Version v1.33.7 (kubespray) ## Sysdump Not attached (production cluster); can provide targeted captures on request. Full monitor drop capture (17 MB) and repeated boot-time snapshots of `endpoint list` / `bpf policy get` / `bpf ipcache list` from inside a locked node are preserved. ## Relevant log output ``` xx drop (Policy denied) flow 0x... to endpoint 0, ifindex 7, file bpf_host.c:865, , identity host->unknown: <node-ip>:39186 -> <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443 tcp SYN xx drop (Policy denied) flow 0x... to endpoint 0, ifindex 2, file bpf_host.c:865, , identity 16777222->unknown: <allowed-admin-ip> -> <node-ip> icmp EchoRequest ``` Agent start with audit mode (the boot that survives): ``` level=warn msg="PolicyAuditMode is enabled. Network policy will not be enforced." level=info msg="Regenerating restored endpoints" restored=0 level=info msg="Creating host endpoint" ``` ## Anything else? - The reboot lockout window matches #25448's "first enforcement" semantics; unlike #25448 the state is permanent because the dropped traffic includes the agent's own apiserver path (chicken-and-egg). - Feature combination overlaps with #31209 (tunnel + KPR + WireGuard + host firewall). - Nothing relevant found in 1.18.7–1.18.13 changelogs. - Happy to run instrumented builds / additional captures on a dedicated test node. ## Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: gateway-api: an apiserver 500 during CRD discovery is treated as "CRDs not installed", disabling Gateway API for the lifetime of the operator
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? Follow-up to #43130 (fixed by #43452 and #44662). Those fixes handle the case where the apiserver is unreachable at the network level. This report is about the remaining hole: an apiserver that answers, but answers 500. `cilium-operator` started while etcd was going through a leader election. The Gateway API CRD discovery GET came back as a server-side error, the operator logged the "resources are not found" message and moved on with Gateway API off. No retry, no backoff warning, no restart. The pod then ran for two hours without a single further gateway-related log line, and the GatewayClass kept the default `Accepted=Unknown / Pending / "Waiting for controller"` status that the upstream CRD ships. Deleting the operator pod fixed it immediately. The CRDs were installed the whole time. The operator said they were not. Expected: a transient server-side failure is retried like a transient network failure, and if it does not clear, the operator exits so the kubelet restarts it. Only a real "the CRD is absent" answer should disable Gateway API silently. ### Mechanism `discoverCRDsWithRetry` splits every discovery failure into "retry" and "the CRDs are not installed" using `isTransientError`, and the second branch is the default: - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/operator/pkg/gateway-api/cell.go#L162-L169 - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/operator/pkg/gateway-api/cell.go#L365-L388 `isTransientError` is an allowlist: four `k8serrors` predicates (`IsServerTimeout`, `IsServiceUnavailable`, `IsTooManyRequests`, `IsTimeout`) plus four `syscall.Errno` values. A 500 carrying `Reason: InternalError` matches none of them, and that is exactly what the apiserver returns when the storage layer fails: `Internal error occurred: etcdserver: leader changed`. Neither does a bare 500 with no reason (`IsUnexpectedServerError`), nor a transport error that is not a plain `syscall.Errno`, such as `http2: client connection lost` or a `Client.Timeout` wrapped in `*url.Error`. Nothing upstream of that narrows it either. `checkCRDs` joins raw client errors, and `CheckCRD` returns the client error untouched; `NotFound` is never distinguished from anything else: - https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/ee26050851a92746155a7319b2554054adb0966c/pkg/k8s/client/crd.go#L15-L37 So the branch that is supposed to mean "the operator looked and the CRD is genuinely absent" is reached by every failure mode the allowlist does not name, and its effect is permanent: `Enabled: false` is returned to the hive, `registerReconcilers` never runs, and no watch, timer or health probe re-enters the path. v1.19 is the same code, verified on the v1.19.7 tag: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/44d55ea770e38bdf4b3a5f5d8079ab311f5a4911/operator/pkg/gateway-api/cell.go#L170-L177 ### Impact Any cluster where the control plane can return a server-side error for a second or two at operator startup. Managed and self-hosted control planes move etcd leadership during upgrades, node replacement and maintenance; the operator is restarted at exactly those moments. The failure is silent — the operator is Running and Ready, the message points at installation docs for CRDs that are already installed, and nothing recovers without a manual pod delete. ### Suggested fix Invert the default. Retry unless the error is specifically `k8serrors.IsNotFound`, i.e. treat "the CRD object does not exist" as the only permanent answer and everything else as retryable. That also removes the need to keep extending the allowlist for every new error shape. If the allowlist stays, it needs at least `IsInternalError` and `IsUnexpectedServerError`, plus a `net.Error` check for transport errors that do not carry an `Errno`. Either way the message on the permanent branch should be reworded: "resources are not found" is what sent me to check the CRDs first, and they were fine. ### How can we reproduce the issue? 1. Install the Gateway API CRDs and enable `gatewayAPI.enabled=true`. 2. Make the apiserver return 500 for `GET /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions/gatewayclasses.gateway.networking.k8s.io` for a few seconds during operator startup. Losing the etcd leader is the natural way; an admission webhook or a proxy that injects 500 works too. 3. Start `cilium-operator` into that window. 4. `kubectl get gatewayclass cilium -o yaml` stays at `Accepted=Unknown`, and the operator log has exactly one gateway line after the discovery message. It never recovers. ### Cilium Version v1.19.5 (vendored chart; behavior verified identical on the v1.19.7 tag) ### Kernel Version 6.18.38 (Talos v1.13.6) ### Kubernetes Version v1.35.6 ### Regression _No response_ ### Sysdump _No response_ ### Relevant log output ```shell level=info msg="Checking for required and optional GatewayAPI resources" requiredGVK="[gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1, Kind=gatewayclasses ...]" level=error msg="Required GatewayAPI resources are not found, please refer to docs for installation instructions" error="etcdserver: leader changed" The absence of the `"Failed to check GatewayAPI CRDs due to transient error, will retry"` warning is the tell: the backoff loop was never entered, the error went straight down the permanent branch on the first attempt. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_ ### Cilium Users Document - [ ] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: NeighborDiscovery leaves stale forwardable-ip entries after node deletion
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Version equal or higher than v1.18.12 and lower than v1.19.0 ### What happened? ## Description A node was deleted: `stage-jfpsf-wn5kt` However, the `forwardable-ip` table still contains an entry owned by the deleted node: ```text cilium shell 'db/get forwardable-ip 10.23.35.70' IP Owners 10.23.35.70 node:default/stage-jfpsf-wn5kt ``` The corresponding kernel neighbor entry also remains: ```text ip neigh | grep 10.23.35.70 10.23.35.70 dev eth0 managed extern_learn INCOMPLETE ``` After some time it may transition to `FAILED`, but it is not removed. The node itself is no longer present, but the stale `forwardable-ip` owner keeps the neighbor entry alive. ## Expected behavior When the node is deleted, NeighborDiscovery should remove the node owner from the `forwardable-ip` table. If there are no remaining owners for the IP, the corresponding desired/kernel neighbor entry should eventually be removed as well. ## Actual behavior The deleted node remains as an owner of the `forwardable-ip` entry: ```text node:default/stage-jfpsf-wn5kt ``` and the kernel neighbor remains: ```text 10.23.35.70 dev eth0 managed extern_learn INCOMPLETE ``` or later: ```text 10.23.35.70 dev eth0 managed extern_learn FAILED ``` The stale neighbor is never cleaned up. ## Impact The stale neighbor causes repeated ARP resolution attempts for an IP that belongs to a deleted node. With multiple stale entries, this generates a significant amount of unnecessary ARP traffic. signals.title: Persistent traffic drops after 1.18.10 → 1.19.5 upgrade - warning log "Skipping named port" for all named-port ingress rules
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues - #38998 (empty policy map after regeneration-retry) — fixed in 1.19.0 via #40255/#40696. - #44855 (empty policy map / wildcard-entry deletion) — requires `policyEnforcementMode: never` but we run with enforcement on. ### Version equal or higher than v1.19.6 and lower than v1.20.0 ### What happened? During an in-place upgrade from 1.18.10 → 1.19.5, cilium pods were restarted as the Daemonset executed a `RollingUpdate`. One of the cilium-agent pods restarted with a bad state, causing all ingress traffic to be dropped for workloads on that node. The issue was only resolved after the pod was manually restarted. Upon upgrade, the problematic cilium-agent pod restarted and restored its existing endpoints (~18 endpoints total). During endpoint restore/regeneration, the agent: 1. Unpinned and recreated every per-endpoint policy map (`cilium_policy_v2_*`). I think this part is expected and benign because I see the `PolicyEntry` value struct changed between [`v1.18.10`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/v1.18.10/pkg/maps/policymap/policymap.go) and [`v1.19.5`](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/v1.19.5/pkg/maps/policymap/policymap.go). 2. Emitted `Skipping named port` logs for the full set of named ports across all workload endpoints. ### Theory Regeneration logs reported success (`regenerated=18 failed=0`), but the named-port ingress allow rules were not programmed based on the `Skipping named port` warnings. Regeneration was never retried, so the endpoints remained misconfigured. ### Additional context * The cluster uses a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy to implement a "default-deny" stance for all workloads * Each workload defines its own CiliumNetworkPolicy to enable ingress and egress and those policies use L4 rules that reference named ports * [Policy enforcement](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/security/policy/intro/) is set to `default` mode ### How can we reproduce the issue? Unsure. It seems to be a race condition give that we saw this behavior on only 3 pods out of 1,800+ pods across various clusters. ### Cilium Version 1.19.5 ### Kernel Version 6.12.94-123.180.amzn2023.x86_64 ### Kubernetes Version 1.33 ### Regression Yes, this seems to be unique to the rule regeneration behavior for version 1.19. Our team cannot say we have definitely observed this problem during previous upgrades. ### Sysdump Not available. The affected `cilium-agent` pod was manually deleted to remediate the outage before a sysdump was captured. ### Relevant log output ```shell time=… level=info msg="Regenerating restored endpoints" module=agent.controlplane.endpoint-restore restored=18 time=… level=info msg="Unpinning map with incompatible properties" \ bpfMapPath=/sys/fs/bpf/tc/globals/cilium_policy_v2_0<ID> \ old="[type LPMTrie keySize 12 valueSize 8 maxEntries 32768 flags 1]" \ new="[type LPMTrie keySize 12 valueSize 12 maxEntries 32768 flags 129]" time=… level=warn msg="Skipping named port" \ ciliumEndpointName=<ns>/<pod> endpointID=<id> k8sPodName=<ns>/<pod> \ subsys=endpoint error="nil map" portName=broker protocol=TCP trafficDirection=ingress time=… level=info msg="Finished regenerating restored endpoints" \ module=agent.controlplane.endpoint-restore regenerated=18 failed=0 ``` ### Anything else? Here is a subset of the configuration from our Helm values file: ``` cni: chainingMode: portmap egressMasqueradeInterfaces: eth+ en+ enableIPv4Masquerade: true encryption: enabled: true nodeEncryption: false type: ipsec eni: enabled: true ipam: mode: eni routingMode: native ``` ### Cilium Users Document - [x] Are you a user of Cilium? Please add yourself to the [Users doc](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/USERS.md) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

signals.title: Gateway API host-network: changing a listener port wedges Envoy in a permanent NACK loop that survives all restarts
signals.text: ## Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues Closest existing issues, both of which I think are distinct: - #45913 — TLS Passthrough listener on a non-standard port silently never binds. Same underlying listener-collapsing behaviour, different symptom (never binds, versus a permanent wedge after a change). - #34982 — one invalid listener stops updates for the others (closed as not planned, v1.16). Related to a secondary effect I hit, but it does not describe the persistence across restarts or the address-set cause. ## What happened? In Gateway API host-network mode, Cilium collapses every listener of a Gateway into a single Envoy listener whose address set carries all the ports (`additionalAddresses`). Changing any listener's port therefore changes that collapsed listener's **address set**, and Envoy cannot update a listener's addresses in place. It rejects the update: ``` error adding listener: 'kube-system/cilium-gateway-default/listener' has duplicate address '0.0.0.0:80,[::]:80,0.0.0.0:443,[::]:443' as existing listener ``` The rejection then becomes **permanent**. It survives restarting Envoy, restarting the agent, restarting both in either order, and restarting the operator. A fresh Envoy connects, binds the old ports, receives the current config, NACKs it, and retries every 15 seconds indefinitely. Deleting the `CiliumEnvoyConfig` does not help either: the operator regenerates it within seconds, so the agent appears to coalesce the delete and recreate into an update of the same resource name, and no removal ever reaches Envoy. ## What I think is going on My reading — and I would not be surprised to be wrong about the mechanism, since I inferred it from behaviour rather than from the source — is that the agent's xDS server replays the last **ACKed** version to each new Envoy stream before offering the current one. That would explain why a fresh Envoy binds the *old* ports before NACKing the new config, and why no amount of restarting escapes it: every new stream re-establishes the same stale state that caused the conflict. What I am confident about is the observable part: the address set changes, Envoy refuses the in-place update, and nothing short of removing the Gateway clears it. ## What does clear it Deleting the **Gateway** itself (not the CEC). The operator then tears the CEC down for real, the agent propagates an actual removal, and Envoy acks it — `lds: remove listener`, ports unbind, ack state clears. Re-applying the Gateway afterwards arrives as a clean ADD carrying the full address set, and every port binds first try in about ten seconds. Routes reattach by `parentRef` name, so deleting and recreating a same-named Gateway needs no route changes. The gateway serves nothing during the window, which was acceptable in my case only because the cutover already had the edge down. ## A related trap while diagnosing this `Gateway.status.listeners` reports `Programmed=True` for the whole duration of the wedge. That condition appears to reflect config generation rather than whether a socket exists, so every status signal looks healthy while nothing is bound. `netstat` on the node and an actual request were the only things that told the truth. If listener status could reflect the Envoy ACK state, this class of problem would be far easier to spot — though I appreciate that may be a larger change than it sounds. ## How to reproduce 1. Cilium with `gatewayAPI.enabled=true` and `gatewayAPI.hostNetwork.enabled=true` 2. A Gateway with an HTTP listener on `:80` and an HTTPS listener on `:443`, both bound and serving 3. Change one listener's port (in my case adding a listener that shifted the collapsed set) 4. Observe the agent log — `completing NACK` — and Envoy — `gRPC config ... rejected` 5. Restart Envoy, the agent, and the operator in any order; the NACK loop resumes each time 6. Delete the Gateway and re-apply it; everything binds immediately ## Cilium Version Observed on **1.20.0**. The cluster has since moved to 1.20.1 and I have not deliberately re-wedged it to confirm the behaviour is unchanged there, since it is now serving real traffic — so treat the 1.20.1 status as untested rather than fixed. ## Kernel Version Talos Linux v1.13.x, single-node cluster, one public IPv4. ## Kubernetes Version v1.36.x ## Regression Not known to be a regression — this was the first time I had used host-network mode, so I have no earlier version to compare against. ## Anything else? Two consequences I have written into my own runbook, in case they are useful for the docs: - Adding a listener on an **existing** port is safe, because the collapsed address set does not change — only the filter chains do. - Adding or changing a **port** is effectively a maintenance event rather than a config tweak, and should be planned like a restart. Happy to gather more detail, test a patch, or re-run the reproduction on a scratch cluster if that would help — I have the environment to hand.

signals.title: preferredIPv6Address() (IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING) ignores deprecated/public-vs-private status, unlike the newer NodeAddress table logic
signals.text: ## Title `preferredIPv6Address()` (IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING) ignores deprecated/public-vs-private status, unlike the newer NodeAddress table logic ## Summary On a node whose direct-routing device carries **two** global-scope IPv6 addresses — a stable ULA and a deprecated (`preferred_lft 0`) SLAAC/GUA address learned via RA — `IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING` (baked into `node_config.h` at agent startup, used by the eBPF datapath for NodePort/LoadBalancer SNAT when forwarding to a non-local backend) can end up set to the **deprecated GUA** instead of the ULA, depending purely on which address the kernel happens to enumerate first. Traffic that gets SNAT'd to that address never receives a reply, since nothing in the surrounding network expects return traffic addressed to it. This reproduces deterministically per-node (not per-packet) — of 4 otherwise-identical nodes in our cluster, 3 have the wrong address baked in and 1 has the correct one, and it's been stable across a full agent restart on the affected nodes (confirmed the fresh agent re-read the same wrong address). ## Environment - Cilium 1.20.1, `kubeProxyReplacement: true`, `Masquerading: IPTables [IPv4: Enabled, IPv6: Enabled]` - Talos Linux (kernel 6.18.44), each node's direct-routing device (`ens18`) has: - a statically-assigned ULA, e.g. `fdc1:e344:ba0a:8:10:2:8:81/64` - a SLAAC address from router advertisements, e.g. `2602:47:193:4c08:be24:11ff:fe0a:da37/64`, **already marked `deprecated` by the kernel** (`preferred_lft 0sec`, `valid_lft` still long) - Backend for the affected Service is an external (non-Cilium-managed) address behind a manually authored `EndpointSlice` — i.e. traffic requires SNAT since it's not a local-pod delivery. ## Reproduction ``` $ ip -6 addr show ens18 inet6 2602:47:193:4c08:be24:11ff:fe0a:da37/64 scope global deprecated dynamic mngtmpaddr proto kernel_ra valid_lft 70257sec preferred_lft 0sec inet6 fdc1:e344:ba0a:8:10:2:8:81/64 scope global valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever ``` ``` $ grep ipv6 /run/cilium/state/globals/node_config.h #define IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING { .addr = { 0x26, 0x2, 0x0, 0x47, 0x1, 0x93, 0x4c, 0x8, 0xbe, 0x24, 0x11, 0xff, 0xfe, 0xa, 0xda, 0x37 } } ``` (decodes to `2602:47:193:4c08:be24:11ff:fe0a:da37` — the deprecated address, not the ULA) Confirmed via `cilium endpoint config <host-ep> Debug=Enabled` + `cilium monitor -vv`: the `to-network` forward for a NodePort SYN to the external backend correctly completes conntrack lookup, backend selection, and DNAT — the *only* wrong part is the chosen source address, matching `IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING` exactly. ## Root cause `pkg/datapath/linux/config/config.go`: ```go func preferredIPv6Address(deviceAddresses []tables.DeviceAddress) netip.Addr { var ip netip.Addr for _, addr := range deviceAddresses { if addr.Addr.Is6() { ip = addr.Addr if !ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() { break } } } return ip } ``` This takes the **first** non-link-local IPv6 address in `deviceAddresses` — whatever order that happens to be in — with no check for `deprecated`/`preferred_lft`, and no public-vs-private preference. The order traces back to raw kernel address-list order, itself a boot-time race between static address configuration and RA-derived SLAAC assignment, so which of the two addresses "wins" is effectively arbitrary per node and stable only until next boot (and not even reliably then). Notably, `pkg/datapath/tables/node_address.go` (the newer `NodeAddress` table, used for BPF masquerade Primary-address selection and `--nodeport-addresses` handling) **already has** explicit public-vs-private preference logic, added specifically for #41866: ```go if addr.Addr.Is6() && !addr.Addr.IsLinkLocalUnicast() { ... if ipv6PublicIndex < 0 && isPublic { ipv6PublicIndex = index } if ipv6PrivateIndex < 0 && !isPublic { ipv6PrivateIndex = index } } ``` `preferredIPv6Address()`/`IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING` never picked up the equivalent treatment — it's a separate, older mechanism operating on the raw `tables.DeviceAddress` list rather than the newer, already-categorized `tables.NodeAddress` table. ## Relation to existing issues - **#36752** ("picks link-local address for IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING") is the same function, but a different, already-fixed edge case: a device with exactly one global address and one link-local, where the pre-fix code picked link-local. Fixed via **#37839**, which is exactly where today's `if !ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() { break }` check comes from. That fix never addressed disambiguating between **multiple valid global addresses**, which is this issue. - **#41866** (BPF masquerade picks wrong host IP with multiple IPs per interface) is the IPv4 analog for a *different* selection path (`NodeAddress`/masquerade Primary selection), already fixed there. This issue is the equivalent gap in the `IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING`/`preferredIPv6Address` path specifically, which wasn't touched by that fix. ## Suggested fix At minimum, skip addresses with `preferred_lft == 0` (deprecated) in `preferredIPv6Address()` when a non-deprecated alternative exists, mirroring what the kernel's own RFC 6724 address selection already does. Ideally, unify this with the `tables.NodeAddress` public/private-preference logic already present for the masquerade Primary-address and `--nodeport-addresses` paths, so `IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING` doesn't have its own, separately-buggy selection logic at all. ## Workaround found `nodePort.enableDynamicSourceLookup` (CLI: `enable-dynamic-source-lookup-nodeport`, added in 1.20.0 per #44625) bypasses this function entirely for NodePort SNAT by doing a live `BPF_FIB_LOOKUP_SRC` kernel FIB lookup per packet instead of using the static `IPV6_DIRECT_ROUTING` value. Not yet confirmed effective in our environment, but the mechanism (kernel FIB) independently gives the correct answer via `ip -6 route get` on our affected nodes.
